RagShortTexts: In 1259 at Skuodas, Samogitian pagan warriors routed the Livonian Order, shattering crusader.

Variants.Content: In 1259, Samogitian pagan warriors led by war-chieftain Alminas raided Courland and ambushed returning Livonian Order contingents at the Battle of Skuodas. Over thirty brother-knights were slaughtered in the dense wetlands, shattering the aura of crusader invincibility.

Chieftains across the Baltic realized that mail-clad heavy cavalry are vulnerable in forested marshlands. Skuodas inspired the Semigallians and Curonians to renounce forced Christian oaths and forge an anti-crusader league.

Samogitians sprang from the brush with barbed spears and broad-headed axes, dismounting armored destriers in knee-deep mud where knightly lances were useless sticks. It was a merciless pagan slaughter.
Forest folk hid baptismal crosses beneath floorboards and poured mead upon sacred roots. The old thunder god answered our prayers; the German monks are flesh and blood, and our woods remain free.
